name: Divar
description: Divar is an Iranian online classifieds platform connecting people advertising goods, property, jobs, and services with potential buyers or respondents. Its city-based organization makes local discovery central to the service, while published advertisements should be distinguished from completed transactions. [s1][s2]

seo.title: Divar: Local Classifieds and Digital Commerce in Iran
seo.description: Explore Divar’s city-based classifieds model, its main categories, and the limits of using advertisements to understand Iranian markets.

content.heading: A digital meeting place for local exchange
content.content:
Divar organizes online classified advertisements around direct contact between people offering something and people searching for it. Its own account dates the platform’s launch to 21 Tir 1391 in Iran’s Solar Hijri calendar and identifies Aghe Pardazan Hooshmand as the company holding the registered brand. The stated purpose was online buying and selling without an intermediary. That description concerns the connection between participants; it does not establish that every advertiser is a private individual or that every transaction takes place entirely within the platform. [s1]

For an international reader, the most useful starting point is the classified advertisement itself. Divar brings together different kinds of offers under a common discovery interface rather than presenting a single retailer’s inventory. Its homepage asks visitors to choose a city before browsing categories, making geography part of the basic service. [s3]

content.heading: How local discovery is organized
content.content:
The inspected Tehran interface separates property, vehicles, digital goods, home and kitchen items, personal belongings, leisure, community listings, industrial equipment, services, and employment. This breadth matters: a search for an apartment, a used appliance, and a job can begin on the same platform, but each represents a different relationship and requires different information. Their presence in a common directory does not make their markets interchangeable. [s2]

Location also operates below the city level. The Tehran page provides a neighborhood filter alongside price, photograph availability, and publication-time controls. Its price filter is labeled in toman. These interface features help explain the platform’s local character, although the Tehran page alone cannot establish that every city has the same depth of listings or identical functionality. [s2]

Divar also documents a web application that can be added to a mobile device’s home screen. This provides another access route alongside its downloadable application; the official explanation describes use through a home-screen icon without separately downloading application updates. [s3]

content.heading: Services around the advertisement
content.content: Divar’s company page describes Karnameh as a complementary automotive service offering vehicle inspection at the customer’s location and assisted selling. This illustrates how a classifieds platform can be accompanied by services addressing questions that an advertisement cannot settle, such as a vehicle’s physical condition. The same page describes Pishgaman as an independent company collaborating on user support. These are specific commercial relationships reported by Divar, rather than evidence that all surrounding businesses belong to one legal entity. [s1]

content.heading: What platform activity can establish
content.content:
Divar’s historical reporting offers evidence of substantial advertising activity, but the units require care. Coverage of its Solar Hijri 1400 report distinguishes devices opening the application, unique advertisers, published advertisements, and advertisement views. These measure different actions: a handset is not necessarily a distinct person, an advertisement is not a completed sale, and a view is not an agreement. [s4]

The report is therefore useful for understanding the platform’s own recorded activity during a defined historical period. It cannot, by itself, establish current market share, the value of completed trade, or representative national prices. A defensible annual chart would require comparable definitions across successive reports. This page does not extend an older company disclosure into an unsupported present-day estimate. [s4]

name: Sheypoor
description: Sheypoor is an Iranian classified-advertising platform covering goods, property, vehicles, employment, and services. Its published interfaces combine local search with advertiser tools, while shareholder reporting describes a business model that includes paid additions to the classifieds service. [s1][s2][s3]

seo.title: Sheypoor: Classified Advertising and Local Markets in Iran
seo.description: Understand Sheypoor’s classifieds categories, advertiser workflow, regional presentation, and the limits of published business metrics.

content.heading: A broad classifieds marketplace
content.content:
Sheypoor presents itself as a platform for advertising goods and services through a website and application. Its main categories include vehicles, property, employment, household goods, electronics, personal items, and business services. The range places individual possessions alongside commercial offers and recruitment: the common feature is an advertisement connecting interested parties, rather than a uniform product sold by Sheypoor itself. [s1]

For readers unfamiliar with Iranian digital commerce, this distinction is useful. A property listing, a vacancy, and an advertisement for a household item all support discovery, but each leaves different questions to be resolved between participants. The platform’s breadth should therefore be understood as a shared advertising infrastructure, not evidence that every category follows the same purchasing or contracting process. [s1][s2]

content.heading: From an offer to a published listing
content.content:
Sheypoor’s inspected help page describes a structured submission process. Advertisers add photographs, choose a category, and enter a title, description, price, and location. City and neighborhood are part of the listing information; optional settings can include contact methods. After submission, advertisers can follow the listing’s status through their account. [s2]

The same documentation distinguishes submitting an advertisement from its publication. Listings enter a review queue, and the account tools support editing and renewal. This is a moderation and publishing workflow; the existence of review does not independently establish the accuracy of every seller’s statement or guarantee the outcome of a later agreement. The help directory also separates payments, visibility promotion, violation reporting, and storefront questions, showing that maintaining an advertisement involves more than its initial submission. [s2]

content.heading: A national directory with regional emphasis
content.content:
The homepage’s property sections distinguish buying an apartment, renting a home, and buying a villa. It highlights searches in Tehran alongside northern cities such as Sari, Babol, Amol, and Rasht, and includes a separate northern-city directory. That presentation gives northern property markets particular visibility within a broader national service. [s1]

These navigation choices are evidence of how Sheypoor organizes discovery. They are not a measurement of regional market share, listing quality, or actual sales. A city appearing prominently on the homepage cannot establish how many households use the service there, and the availability of a category does not demonstrate that every locality has equivalent supply. [s1]

content.heading: Paid features and the limits of growth claims
content.content:
Pomegranate Investment’s annual report for the period ending April 2024 describes Sheypoor as a general classifieds platform with particular regional and category strengths, including property. It reports the addition of paid features and a decline in total users and sessions during Solar Hijri 1402, alongside stronger revenue performance in a business segment. This is a shareholder’s account and should be attributed accordingly. [s3]

The combination is instructive: audience growth and revenue growth are separate questions. A platform can obtain more income from paid services while recording fewer visits or users. Neither measure alone establishes whether customers completed more satisfactory transactions. The inspected material does not support a continuous annual series with stable definitions, so it is more accurate to preserve this dated business context than to manufacture a trend from unrelated audience claims. [s3]

name: Home Service Platforms
description: Home service platforms help households find providers for tasks such as cleaning, repairs, installation, and moving. Iranian examples including Achareh and Sanjagh organize requests and provider discovery, while their published documentation distinguishes the platform’s matching role from the work performed by individual service providers. [s1][s2][s3][s4]

seo.title: Home Service Platforms in Iran: Requests, Providers, and Trust
seo.description: Explore how Iranian home service platforms organize cleaning and repair requests, compare providers, and describe their responsibilities.

content.heading: Connecting a household task with a provider
content.content:
Home service platforms organize work that ultimately happens in a physical place. A household may discover a provider online, but cleaning, repairing an appliance, or installing equipment still depends on a person arriving with appropriate skills and an agreed understanding of the task. Achareh’s inspected service directory includes cleaning, building work, repairs, and moving; its homepage presents a sequence of choosing a service or specialist, placing an order, and receiving service at the location. [s1]

This makes the category more specific than general online advertising. The digital service structures a request around work to be performed, although the exact matching and agreement process varies by platform. Achareh and Sanjagh illustrate different presentations of that process; they should not be treated as an exhaustive directory of Iranian providers. [s1][s2]

content.heading: Requests, estimates, and customer choice
content.content:
Sanjagh’s explanation begins with questions about the requested task. It says the platform forwards the request to suitable providers, who can submit proposals. The customer compares estimated costs, previous customer ratings and comments, provider background, and messages before choosing whom to engage. Its documentation also says the customer’s telephone number is shared with a provider only at the customer’s request. These statements describe the platform’s published process, rather than independently measured performance. [s2]

The distinction between an estimate and a final agreement is central. A proposal helps a household compare offers, while the eventual scope and price still require agreement. Sanjagh’s terms describe negotiations, pricing, and contracts as matters between the service recipient and provider. That is the company’s stated allocation of responsibilities; it is not a determination of how a court would resolve a particular dispute. [s4]

content.title: Sanjagh’s documented request and selection process
content.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Household describes the task"] -->|"Submits request"| B["Sanjagh routes the request"]
  B -->|"Invites suitable providers"| C["Providers submit proposals"]
  C -->|"Offers estimates and profile information"| D["Household compares proposals"]
  D -->|"Selects a provider and discusses details"| E["Customer and provider agree the work"]
```
content.summary: The arrows show information and selection steps described by Sanjagh. They do not imply that the platform employs the provider, fixes the final price, or guarantees the work.

content.heading: What a profile or platform promise establishes
content.content:
Ratings and provider profiles can make prior experience visible, but their meaning requires qualification. Sanjagh’s safety guide encourages readers to consider completed jobs alongside ratings and to inspect the documents associated with a verification mark. It explicitly says the platform does not approve or reject the quality of providers’ work. Its recommendation to record the work’s timing, total price, and details reflects the importance of a clear agreement beyond the profile itself. [s5]

Achareh’s terms likewise describe a software service connecting customers and specialists and characterize the service agreement as a separate arrangement between those participants. The terms state that specialists can accept or reject requests. These published descriptions help explain the marketplace model, but cannot establish actual employment classification or remove any responsibilities that applicable law might impose. [s3]

content.heading: Local availability and the evidence still needed
content.content:
Achareh presents city-specific entry points, while the inspected Sanjagh directory was a Tehran page containing household repair, cleaning, installation, and moving categories. This supports describing service discovery as geographically organized. It does not establish that every listed task is available in every neighborhood or at every requested time. [s1][s6]

The category’s significance lies in making requests, offers, and provider histories easier to compare. Whether it also improves prices, worker earnings, punctuality, or dispute resolution requires outcome evidence beyond service menus and terms. The inspected sources do not establish those effects, and no national annual series is supplied here. [s1][s2][s4][s5]
